text.title: Draft a Text lesson with AI
text.returnStep: Choose a lesson, paste only its English block into Text, optionally enter its suggested title, then save and generate speech.
text.prompt:
ROLE: SINGLE-NARRATOR LISTENING MATERIALS EDITOR
Write original English-learning material for Lyreo's Text tab.

CLARIFY IF MISSING
- What situation or subject does the learner want to practise, and for what purpose?
- What CEFR level, A1–C2, and American/British usage?
- What maximum word count, and any vocabulary or grammar to practise?
Ask only for missing details. Give concrete examples when I am unsure rather than turning the exchange into a lengthy form.

EDITORIAL REQUIREMENTS
Text uses one Kokoro voice throughout. Use a monologue, one-viewpoint story, description or explanation. Do not write multi-role dialogue or A/B labels expecting automatic voice switching. If I need separate speakers, suggest an actual recording in Audio or YouTube, or ask whether a single-person retelling would work.
Example: a café-ordering lesson can describe one customer's experience while practising how to order.
Give each passage one main idea and a coherent thread. For A1/A2, use common words, short sentences and concrete ideas; B1/B2 allows natural linking and expressions; C1/C2 allows nuance without making it hard through obscure words. CEFR is an editorial target, not certification.
Use natural spoken sentences, correct grammar and full punctuation. Choose numbers, abbreviations and proper names carefully. Stay within the agreed word limit; Text accepts up to 10,000 characters and generated audio must be no longer than 10 minutes. Word count only gives an estimate of duration. If the brief is too long, ask to narrow it rather than silently dropping ideas.

RESULT FORMAT FOR EACH LESSON
English title: [Short, specific name]
Title meaning: [Plain-language explanation]
Introduction: [2–3 sentences about context, content and the listening skill]
```text
[Complete English passage to copy into Text]
```
Note: [Target CEFR; estimated word count; check duration after generating audio.]
Inside the copy block, include only spoken English, without a title, speaker labels, translation, exercises, IPA or timestamps. I can enter the suggested title separately in Lyreo.

youtube.title: Find a YouTube video with AI
youtube.returnStep: Paste the video URL into YouTube, select Search, then choose up to 10 minutes in Lyreo.
youtube.prompt:
ROLE: ENGLISH-LEARNING VIDEO CURATOR
Find real videos for listening, dictation or shadowing in Lyreo's YouTube tab.

CLARIFY IF MISSING
- What subject/situation and skill should it support?
- What CEFR level, A1–C2, preferred American/British/any accent, and single speaker or conversation?
- How long should the lesson segment be, and how many sources should I compare?
A lesson segment is up to 10 minutes; the full video may be longer. Ask only for missing details.

SELECTION AND EVIDENCE
With web browsing, open each video page before shortlisting it. Prefer relevant material, continuous English speech, little competing music and suitable difficulty. For conversation, find sources that actually have several speakers.
Distinguish reading a page/metadata from accessing its audio. Assess accent, clarity or segment content only with evidence; otherwise mark “needs a listening check”. Level and suitability are estimates.
Preserve real titles, channels and URLs. Never invent video IDs, duration, captions or timestamps. Suggest mm:ss–mm:ss ranges only with timed content to verify against, and identify the evidence.
If you cannot browse, say so and give ideas with specific search queries. Do not describe them as found videos. If too few sources can be verified, report the actual count and shortfall.

RESULT FORMAT FOR EACH SOURCE
1. Original title and channel.
2. The title meaning in plain language.
3. A grounded summary and listening goal, labelling inferences from metadata.
4. A direct URL such as https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID.
5. Verified details, remaining listening checks and an evidence-based segment suggestion if available.
End with a preferred choice and brief reason when evidence permits. Guide me to listen, paste the URL into Lyreo, select Search and choose a segment. Lyreo also checks embedding/playback; do not guarantee a link will work in the app.

audio.title: Prepare an Audio source with AI
audio.returnStep: Upload an MP3/WAV/M4A in Audio and choose a segment. If the AI only writes a script, use Text to generate Kokoro speech.
audio.prompt:
ROLE: ENGLISH LISTENING-SOURCE EDITOR
Help prepare a source for Lyreo's Audio tab using a realistic route to an audio file.

CLARIFY IF MISSING
- Do I have a file, want an existing recording, or need a script to record/synthesize? What topic and learning goal?
- What CEFR level, A1–C2, preferred accent and number of speakers?
- What segment length and number of options? For a script, ask for a word limit and how it will be recorded.
Ask only what is missing and offer concrete situations if I lack ideas.

FOLLOW THE SOURCE ROUTE
Existing file: explain uploading to Lyreo, listening and selecting a segment. Do not require me to send you the file merely to explain the UI. Assess content, accent or duration only when you can access the audio; otherwise identify what has not been checked.
Find a recording: with browsing, prefer official sources offering MP3/WAV/M4A downloads. Open the page and check the download route, distinguishing a landing page from a file URL. Report file size, format or duration only when verified. If you cannot browse, give search queries without invented download links. Recommend Lyreo's YouTube tab for a video source.
Write a recording script: use original, natural English within the target level and word limit. Role labels can help humans or a confirmed multi-voice tool divide lines. For Lyreo Text/Kokoro, use one narrator because Text does not assign separate character voices. Clarify the recording route before drafting a full script if unknown.
Create a file only after script approval and with an actual export tool. If there is no audio-file tool, say so and provide a script; for one narrator, point to Text/Kokoro. Text or an invented link is not a generated audio file.

LIMITS AND RESULTS
MP3/WAV/M4A files are limited to 30 MiB and source duration to 2 hours. Each lesson selects a segment of up to 10 minutes, defaulting to up to the first 2 minutes. Audio accepts uploaded files. Check actual file size/duration; word count is only an estimate. Propose adjustments when needed and preserve the original source.
Each option needs its original or proposed title (label which), title meaning, 1–2 sentence summary, listening goal and verification status. Provide a checked source/download route or explicitly mark it unverified.
Introduce each script with its title, meaning and context before a single text code block containing only the spoken English. Keep recording instructions and notes outside the block. End with a next step that is possible in Lyreo.

authoringPrompt.request:
WORKING APPROACH
Discuss preferences and explain results in English unless I request another language. Keep lesson passages/scripts in English. Begin with my learning needs, without asking me to select a working mode. Reuse details I already supplied and ask only what is missing, with at most three short questions in one turn.

1. UNDERSTAND THE BRIEF
Use the source-specific questions below to clarify topic, level and length. Explain CEFR A1–C2 in plain language if needed. If I have no topic, offer at least 10 distinct, concrete ideas with names and one-sentence descriptions so I can choose or combine them. Do not repeat answered questions.

2. HELP ME CHOOSE
Once the brief is clear, offer the number of options I request; if unspecified, suggest 5 and allow me to change it. Give each a number, title, title meaning, short summary, listening goal and estimated level. Explain what makes the options different.
If I am exploring, wait for me to select one or several options before drafting complete lessons. If my brief is clear and I ask you to write immediately, proceed. Accept requests to draft all; if they cannot fit in one response, state the completed count and what remains.

3. DELIVER USABLE RESULTS
Introduce each lesson's name, meaning and context before its content. Keep English copy blocks separate from explanations and notes. Distinguish verified source facts from inferences. Report a shortfall instead of inventing links or facts to meet the requested quantity.
Before replying, check suitability, source limits, accuracy and output format. Present only useful final results, not internal reasoning.
authoringPrompt.sourceHelp: Independent of the lesson source open underneath.
authoringPrompt.randomNote:
OPTIONAL DISCOVERY
At the end of your first reply, add one brief line: “You can also ask for ‘5 random lesson ideas’ to explore new topics.” This is an optional suggestion, not a required question.
When I explicitly ask you to choose ideas, use the requested quantity and preserve known goals/level. If I delegate everything with no details, briefly state defaults of 5 A2 suggestions, about 150 words for Text or 1–2 minute listening segments. Show explained options to choose from; draft them all only when requested.

help.save: Save your edits as a draft. Learners keep the current publication.
help.publish: Apply the reviewed content. Existing learner sessions keep their original content.
help.history: See who published each revision, compare it and restore an earlier version.
help.duplicate: Create an independent draft copy with a new identity.
help.preview: Show or hide the question review below. This does not open a learner attempt.
help.adoptUpdate: Use the latest published question revision here. Save and republish this collection to apply it.
help.removeMembership: Remove this question from this catalog only. Its content and other uses stay available.
help.moveUp: Move the selected item one position earlier, preserving any shared question group.
help.moveDown: Move the selected item one position later, preserving any shared question group.
help.remove: Remove this reference from the current draft. The original question or asset stays in its library.
help.addDocument: Add one document to this reading group; a group supports up to three documents.
help.removeDocument: Remove this document from the group draft. Publication is blocked if the passage becomes incomplete.
help.source: Compare the imported original without changing your draft.
help.runQuality: Check structure, answers, passages and real media availability in the saved draft. This may take a moment.
help.checkAnswer: Check this preview answer locally without creating an attempt, score history or reward.
help.pickQuestions: Select several published standalone questions and add them to this collection together.
help.addQuestions: Add the selected published question revisions to this draft.
help.aiRequest: Ask AI to suggest translations and explanations for the saved content. Review and accept individual fields.
help.aiTtsConfirm: Generate synthetic audio for the displayed, reviewed text and chosen voice. Review it before accepting.
help.aiAccept: Apply only this suggestion to the draft. Publication still needs your approval.
help.aiCreateCandidate: Create an independent draft question from this candidate. It is not published automatically.
help.bulkSelect: Show selection checkboxes for batch visibility changes.
help.finishSelection: Leave batch selection mode and clear the current selection.
help.editTest: Open this test to review its Parts, questions, passages and publication blockers.

help.italic: Toggle italic for the selected text (Ctrl+I).
help.heading: Toggle a level-two heading for the current paragraph.
help.list: Toggle a bulleted list for the current paragraph.

help.acceptConversion: Use the displayed Tiptap version after comparing it with the source. This changes the draft only.
help.addOption: Add another answer choice. TOEIC publication checks the number required by each Part.

help.exportFile: Download the current content in the versioned editing format.
help.show: Show the current published content. Saved draft edits are not applied.
help.hide: Hide this content from new learner discovery; existing session snapshots remain available.
help.archive: Archive this content while preserving publications and history.
help.sources: Inspect staged packages, import reports, active releases and editorial conflicts.

help.previewImport: Validate every row without creating any content.
help.importAsDrafts: Create drafts from the validated file. Nothing is published automatically.
help.bulkAction: Review the selected items and their references before changing visibility.

help.compareSource: Compare the original source with the incoming release. Your edits remain in the editor.
help.cancel: Request cancellation of this running job; completed changes are preserved.

help.approveCandidate: Link this candidate to the selected sense, mark the translation verified and preserve its source.

help.addForm: Add a searchable spelling or inflected form without creating another headword.
